paper_metadata.title: Comparing Quantum Circuit Born Machines and Restricted Boltzmann Machines for Generative Modelling of Financial Data

experiments.description: Simulated quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) trained on correlated FX currency-pair log-return data using Sinkhorn divergence, evaluated across multiple problem sizes and precisions on Rigetti Forest simulators.

algorithm.variant: Quantum circuit Born machine with hardware-efficient ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient, native Rigetti CZ + Ry layers

hyperparameters.parameterization: single-qubit rotations only; two-qubit gates unparameterized

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Currency-pair spot prices are discretized into binary strings; each currency pair is represented with j bits of precision, giving i*j qubits for i pairs.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize Sinkhorn divergence between model distribution p_theta(x) and data distribution T.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic data generation for correlated foreign-exchange currency pairs.

dataset_specification.description: Daily log-returns of 4 currency pairs between 1999 and 2019; examples in the paper focus on 2 pairs (EUR/USD and GBP/USD), 3 pairs, and 4 pairs at varying bit precisions.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Spot prices converted to 16-bit binary values; log-returns used for the financial dataset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Binary discretization of spot prices; selection of sublattices matching chip topology for hardware runs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Model quality evaluated with a random forest discriminator (1000 estimators) and QQ plots.

speedup_claims.conditions: Simulated QCBM on correlated FX currency-pair log-return data across multiple problem sizes and precisions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports that the simulated Born machine always at least matches the RBM and demonstrates superior performance as the model scales, but no asymptotic or runtime speedup is claimed.

experiments.description: Restricted Boltzmann machine baseline trained on the same FX dataset, with bias-only training and random fixed weights, used as the classical comparator to the QCBM across the same problem sizes.

algorithm.variant: Restricted Boltzmann machine with bias-only training

hyperparameters.sampling_method: QxSQA simulated quantum annealer / PIMC-based sampling

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random fixed weights; biases trained from initialization not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Visible nodes correspond to binary variables representing discretized currency-pair values; hidden nodes added to match parameter count with QCBM.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize log-likelihood of training data under the RBM distribution.

problem_instance.description: Same FX synthetic data generation task as the QCBM, evaluated for 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 bits of precision and for 2, 3, and 4 currency pairs.

dataset_specification.description: Daily log-returns of 4 currency pairs between 1999 and 2019; 2-pair examples include EUR/USD and GBP/USD.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Spot prices converted to 16-bit binary values; hidden-node count scaled to match QCBM parameter count.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random fixed weights; hidden nodes chosen to match QCBM parameter count; sampling via QxSQA.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Random forest discriminator evaluation; QQ plots; comparison against QCBM outputs.

speedup_claims.conditions: RBM baseline on the same FX dataset
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the classical comparator itself; no speedup claim is associated with it.

experiments.description: Physical-hardware QCBM experiments on Rigetti Aspen-7 and Aspen-8 sublattices, including the largest reported 28-qubit instance, trained with Sinkhorn divergence.

algorithm.variant: Quantum circuit Born machine on Rigetti QPU sublattices
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient, native entanglement structure with CZ gates and Ry rotations

hyperparameters.parameterization: single-qubit rotations only; two-qubit gates unparameterized

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary strings represent discretized currency-pair values; problem sizes include (i,j) = (2,2), (2,3), (2,4), (2,5), (2,6), (4,7), and a 28-qubit instance for 4 currency pairs at 7 bits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize Sinkhorn divergence between generated and target distributions.

problem_instance.description: Same FX dataset, but executed on real Rigetti hardware sublattices matched to the chip topology.

dataset_specification.description: Daily log-returns of 4 currency pairs between 1999 and 2019; hardware runs shown for 2, 3, and 4 currency pairs at varying precisions.

problem_instance.classical_preprocessing: Selection of Aspen-7 and Aspen-8 sublattices; binary discretization of spot prices.
problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Random forest discriminator; entanglement-capacity analysis; QQ plots for selected cases.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Mapping problem sizes to hardware-native sublattices; using native CZ connectivity.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluation with random forest discriminator; mean and standard deviation over 5 independent training runs.

speedup_claims.conditions: Physical-hardware QCBM on Rigetti Aspen-7 and Aspen-8 sublattices, including the 28-qubit instance
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports partial training of the largest instance to date and notes that performance is likely limited by hardware errors; no speedup is claimed.

experiments.description: Alternative QCBM training on small instances using maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) instead of Sinkhorn divergence.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same binary currency-pair encoding as the main QCBM experiments.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize MMD between model and data distributions.

problem_instance.description: Small FX instances used for appendix comparison of training objectives.

dataset_specification.description: 2 currency pairs at 2 and 4 bits of precision; small qubit counts (4, 6, 8) in appendix figures.

speedup_claims.conditions: Appendix comparison of QCBM training objectives using MMD
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit speedup claim is made; the appendix states MMD was considered as an alternative cost function.

experiments.description: Alternative QCBM training using an adversarial discriminator objective, compared against Sinkhorn divergence and MMD on small instances.

algorithm.variant: QCBM trained adversarially against a discriminator

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same binary currency-pair encoding as the main QCBM experiments.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Adversarial generator objective relative to a discriminator trained to distinguish real and generated samples.

problem_instance.description: Small FX instances used for appendix comparison of training objectives.

dataset_specification.description: 2 currency pairs at 2 and 4 bits of precision; small qubit counts (4, 6, 8) in appendix figures.

problem_instance.classical_postprocessing: Discriminator-based evaluation and retraining each iteration.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random forest discriminator retrained from scratch at each generator iteration.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison against Sinkhorn-trained and MMD-trained QCBMs.

speedup_claims.conditions: Appendix adversarial training of QCBM against a discriminator
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes adversarial training was slower than Sinkhorn divergence and therefore did not receive increased focus.
